I have $26 and two unmortgaged properties. I am analyzing p1's holdings to decide on a post-turn action.

The red property set is split between us. I own Kentucky and Illinois. p1 owns Tennessee, Indiana, and Pennsylvania.

p1 holds a light blue monopoly with hotels, plus Tennessee, Indiana, Pennsylvania Avenue, and Short Line. p3 has an unbuilt yellow set and dark blue properties with three houses each.

p4 has $455 cash and a pink monopoly with three houses each. p3 has $54 cash. My position is dire. I cannot build or acquire Indiana to complete the red set.

Mortgaging both properties would yield $230. I am weighing a trade for Indiana against simply ending the turn. p1 already holds a light blue monopoly with hotels, so they may be eager to acquire Indiana.

Trading one red property for Indiana would not complete the set. I would still need to acquire Kentucky. p1 could also gain a second monopoly by receiving both of my reds.

I cannot afford Indiana with my current cash. p1 previously rejected a $200-250 offer, and I have no other assets to trade. p4 has $455 but lacks appealing holdings for me. p3 also has nothing I need. I will not sell or mortgage my reds, as that would either hand p1 the set or destroy my only path to a monopoly. I must survive this turn without trading.

I have ruled out any trade with p1. I will end the turn.
